title: Fix CPU call-targets clap gpu-list dependency
description: CPU call-targets panics in clap debug assertions because shared CallTargetsArgs uses required_unless_present_any referencing gpu_list, which exists only on call-targets-gpu. Split or adjust CLI argument requirements so CPU call-targets help and parsing work while GPU --gpu-list remains standalone.
acceptance_criteria: cargo run --features wgpu -- call-targets --help no longer panics; call-targets still requires input/bamlist and reference; call-targets-gpu --gpu-list remains standalone; tests/checks pass.
close_reason: Removed gpu_list-dependent clap requirements from shared CallTargetsArgs and rely on runtime validation after GPU --gpu-list exits. Verified CPU call-targets help no longer panics, call-targets reports missing --reference normally, and call-targets-gpu --gpu-list remains standalone.

title: Fix GPU counts buffer write usage
description: call-targets-gpu panics during counts buffer initialization because create_chunk_states calls queue.write_buffer on a buffer created with COPY_SRC | STORAGE but not COPY_DST. Add the required usage flag and verify the wgpu test suite.
acceptance_criteria: call-targets-gpu no longer panics at Queue::write_buffer during chunk state creation; wgpu feature tests pass.
close_reason: Added COPY_DST to the GPU counts buffer usage because create_chunk_states initializes it with Queue::write_buffer. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Classify paired calls in CPU output
description: Use paired tumor/normal sample evidence to classify and filter call-targets output for one tumor/normal pair.
design: After alt selection, compute tumor/normal DP, alt count, and AF for the selected ALT. Require tumor min alt count/fraction and normal max alt count/fraction plus optional min normal depth. Add INFO fields PAIR, SOMATIC, TUMOR_AF, NORMAL_AF, TUMOR_ALT_COUNT, NORMAL_ALT_COUNT, TUMOR_DP, NORMAL_DP. Preserve existing FORMAT output for all samples.
acceptance_criteria: CPU call-targets paired mode emits only paired-passing records with paired INFO fields; unpaired mode output is unchanged; tests cover pass/fail threshold behavior.
close_reason: Implemented paired tumor/normal filtering in the shared VCF output path. Paired mode now evaluates the selected ALT against tumor min count/fraction, normal max count/fraction, and optional normal min depth; passing records get PAIR, SOMATIC, TUMOR_AF, NORMAL_AF, TUMOR_ALT_COUNT, NORMAL_ALT_COUNT, TUMOR_DP, and NORMAL_DP INFO annotations. Unpaired output remains unchanged. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Add paired calling CLI and role validation
description: Add initial paired calling CLI flags for one tumor/normal pair and validate sample role names against collected sample names.
design: Extend CallTargetsArgs with --pair tumor=SAMPLE,normal=SAMPLE, tumor thresholds, normal thresholds, and optional min normal depth. Parse into a small PairedCallingConfig after sample collection. Validate both samples exist and differ. No output behavior change in this slice beyond validation/help/tests.
acceptance_criteria: call-targets and call-targets-gpu expose paired flags; invalid pair specs and unknown samples fail with clear errors; tests cover parser and validation.
close_reason: Added paired calling CLI flags and role validation. --pair tumor=S,normal=S plus tumor/normal threshold flags are parsed through shared CallTargetsArgs, so they are visible for call-targets and call-targets-gpu. prepare_call_targets validates sample names exist and differ, stores PairedCallingConfig for later classification, and tests cover parser/validation plus CPU/GPU help exposure. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Implement initial exact-key VCF annotation
description: Add an initial varlock annotate subcommand for exact CHROM/POS/REF/ALT annotation from one or more VCF-like databases. This first slice can load database VCFs into memory and stream/copy the input VCF while appending INFO annotations.
design: CLI: varlock annotate --input calls.vcf.gz --database name=path.vcf.gz --annotation name:SRC=DEST[,SRC=DEST] --output calls.annotated.vcf.gz. Parse headers and records as tab-delimited VCF text. Key records by CHROM, POS, REF, ALT for single ALT records initially; skip multi-ALT DB records or split them if straightforward. Preserve input header, add INFO header lines for DEST fields, add source provenance, append annotations to INFO on exact key hits. Use bgzip output. Indexed lookup and normalization remain follow-up work.
acceptance_criteria: Annotate subcommand exists; exact-key VCF database annotation works for simple one-ALT records; multiple databases and field mappings are namespaced by user-provided destination fields; tests cover hit/no-hit behavior; cargo test passes.
close_reason: Implemented initial varlock annotate subcommand for exact CHROM/POS/REF/ALT annotation from VCF-like databases. Supports repeated --database NAME=VCF and --annotation NAME:SRC=DEST mappings, bgzipped output, header/provenance insertion, exact single-ALT matches, and tests for hits/no-hits, mappings, multi-ALT skip behavior, and flag INFO fields. Verified cargo test, cargo test --features wgpu, and annotate --help.

title: Document current varlock functionality in README
description: Add a repository README that explains current varlock functionality, build commands, CPU/GPU call-targets usage, sample handling, target/no-target behavior, output files, and examples including multi-GPU static-target execution.
acceptance_criteria: README.md exists and reflects the current CLI behavior; examples include CPU calling, GPU calling, no-target calling, RG mapping/default sample behavior, GPU listing/selection, filters, and output/index notes.
close_reason: Added README.md documenting current CPU/GPU calling functionality, inputs, samples/RG mapping, filters, outputs/indexes, GPU selection/multi-GPU static target examples, no-target caveats, logging, and roadmap examples for intersection and annotation.

title: Introduce GPU runtime set
description: Refactor call-targets-gpu setup from a single GpuRuntime/GpuAggregateKernel pair to a small runtime set that can hold one kernel per selected adapter. Keep execution using the first runtime until sharding lands.
design: Create a GpuExecutionContext or GpuWorkerRuntime struct containing runtime, kernel, tier, matrix budget, max_obs_upload, and flush threshold. Build Vec<...> from selected adapters. Existing call paths should use runtimes[0] initially. This keeps the later sharding patch focused.
acceptance_criteria: Setup supports multiple initialized runtimes internally; single-runtime behavior and logs remain sensible; no aggregation behavior changes; tests pass.
close_reason: Refactored GPU setup to initialize a Vec of worker runtimes, each with runtime, kernel, tier, matrix budget, max_obs_upload, and flush threshold. Existing aggregation paths use the first worker for now, preserving behavior while enabling later sharding. Verified cargo test, cargo test --features wgpu, and --gpu-list smoke.

title: Make no-target GPU streaming coordinate-window correct
description: Replace no-target observation-threshold flushing with coordinate/window flushing so sites do not cross arbitrary batches and max-depth semantics remain deterministic before multi-GPU no-target sharding.
design: Scan covered observations in coordinate order per input/reference where possible and flush only complete windows. If a site can appear in more than one worker/window, aggregate raw counts before max-depth capping or route all observations for a site to one window. Add tests proving output is independent of flush threshold for the same observations.
acceptance_criteria: No-target GPU output is invariant to flush threshold on focused tests; sites are not capped in multiple independent flushes; tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed the no-target GPU flush-threshold correctness risk by accumulating flushed batch counts uncapped and applying max_depth once after all no-target flushes. This preserves the same cap result as a single aggregate batch without needing arbitrary observation batches to align to coordinate windows. Added a regression test for split-vs-single cap equivalence. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Support selecting multiple GPU adapters
description: Extend call-targets-gpu adapter selection from one adapter to an ordered set. Add CLI support for repeated --gpu-index or a --gpu-indices list while preserving --gpu-index/--gpu-name single-adapter behavior. Do not change aggregation execution yet; this is the selection foundation for multi-GPU sharding.
design: Represent selection as a list of adapter indices after resolving user input. Keep --gpu-list as the source of stable per-run indices. Reject duplicate indices, out-of-range indices, and mixing multi-index selection with --gpu-name. Default remains a single HighPerformance adapter through request_adapter. Add tests for parsing and selector resolution.
acceptance_criteria: call-targets-gpu can resolve zero, one, or multiple explicit GPU adapter indices; default single-GPU behavior is unchanged; selector validation has unit coverage; cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu pass.
close_reason: Made --gpu-index repeatable and changed GPU selector resolution to produce an ordered adapter index set with duplicate, conflict, and range validation. Current single-runtime initialization rejects multi-index execution clearly until runtime-set support lands. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Add explicit GPU adapter selection
description: Support multi-GPU machines by listing available wgpu adapters and selecting a specific adapter instead of relying only on request_adapter HighPerformance policy. Add CLI options for --gpu-list, --gpu-index, and --gpu-name. Preserve existing default behavior when no selector is provided.
design: Extend GPU initialization to enumerate adapters for the selected backend. If --gpu-list is set, print adapter index, name, type, backend, vendor/device IDs, and limits then exit before opening BAM inputs. If --gpu-index is set, choose that enumerated adapter. If --gpu-name is set, choose the first adapter whose name contains the substring case-insensitively. Reject using both index and name. Keep existing request_adapter behavior as the default path so current behavior remains stable.
acceptance_criteria: call-targets-gpu exposes --gpu-list, --gpu-index, and --gpu-name; invalid selectors return clear errors; default behavior remains request_adapter HighPerformance; tests cover selector validation and adapter selection helpers.
close_reason: Added --gpu-list, --gpu-index, and --gpu-name for call-targets-gpu. GPU listing enumerates compatible adapters and exits without call inputs; explicit index/name selection uses enumerated adapters while default behavior remains HighPerformance request_adapter. Added selector tests and verified cargo test plus cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Stream no-target GPU aggregation in chunks
description: Optimize call-targets-gpu when no target BED is provided so covered-site discovery and aggregation do not require buffering all observations for the full run. The current path scans all covered observations into memory, sorts/dedupes every site key, remaps observations, then aggregates. This should become bounded-memory chunked aggregation suitable for WGS/high-depth BAMs.
design: Use coordinate windows as the streaming boundary. Keep per-reference/window covered observations in memory, build a local sorted site map for the window, run the existing GPU aggregate kernel for that window, materialize counts, merge into output counts, then release the window. Preserve the existing static-target GPU path. Initial implementation can require coordinate-sorted BAM input for the no-target streaming path; later work can support unsorted input by spilling/sorting or falling back. Add verbose metrics for windows, sites, observations, peak pending observations, and flush counts.
acceptance_criteria: No-target call-targets-gpu processes data with bounded memory by flushing coordinate windows; static target mode remains unchanged; output matches the existing no-target GPU behavior on focused tests; default and wgpu feature test suites pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Support call-targets-gpu without target BED
description: GPU mode currently falls back to CPU when --targets is omitted because the static target site map would expand the whole reference. Add a no-target GPU path that discovers covered sites from scanned observations and aggregates those covered positions on the GPU.
close_reason: Added call-targets-gpu no-target mode by scanning covered positions, remapping covered observations to dense site indices, and reusing GPU aggregation. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Fallback call-targets to one sample without RG/SM mapping
description: call-targets currently errors when no --rg-map is provided and BAM headers do not expose RG/SM samples. In that case, process all records as a single sample instead of failing.
close_reason: Implemented single-sample fallback for call-targets without RG/SM mappings and verified with cargo test.

title: Implement gpu/scan.rs — parallel BAM scan workers with observation emission
description:
Create src/call_targets/gpu/scan.rs to spawn one thread per BAM input, each scanning its BAM and emitting packed Observations into a shared synchronous channel.

## ScanEvent enum
```rust
pub(crate) enum ScanEvent {
    Batch {
        input_idx: usize,
        frontier_site_idx: u32,    // lowest unprocessed site_idx for this input
        observations: Vec<Observation>,
    },
    Progress {
        input_idx: usize,
        frontier_site_idx: u32,
    },
    Done {
        input_idx: usize,
        skipped_rg: usize,
        skipped_flags: usize,
    },
}
```

## scan_bam_worker(input_idx, path, params, target_sites, frontier_index, scan_tx)
One thread per BAM. Reads records using the same filtering logic as pileup.rs (should_skip_record, record_sample, MAPQ filter). Per qualifying record:

1. For each base in target (using CIGAR walk from pileup_record logic):
   - Look up site_idx via target_sites.site_index(ref_id, pos1)
   - If Some(site_idx): emit Observation { site_idx, sample_base: (sample_idx << 2) | base_idx }
   - Add to current batch buffer
2. Every SCAN_BATCH_OBSERVATIONS (100,000) observations, flush a Batch event via blocking send
3. Every FRONTIER_PROGRESS_STEP sites processed (every time frontier advances by 20,000 sites), emit a Progress event via non-blocking try_send (drop if channel full)
4. At EOF: flush remaining observations as Batch, then send Done event

## ScanWorkerParams struct
```rust
pub(crate) struct ScanWorkerParams {
    pub(crate) rg_to_sm: Arc<HashMap<String, String>>,
    pub(crate) sample_index: Arc<HashMap<String, usize>>,
    pub(crate) min_mapq: u8,
    pub(crate) min_baseq: u8,
    pub(crate) max_depth: u32,
}
```

## spawn_scan_workers(inputs, params, target_sites, frontier_index) -> (Receiver<ScanEvent>, Vec<JoinHandle>)
Channel capacity = max(32, inputs.len() * 4) — enough buffer without unbounded memory.
Spawn one thread per input, each calling scan_bam_worker with its own clone/Arc of shared state.
notes: The CIGAR walking logic is nearly identical to pileup_record in pileup.rs — consider extracting a shared base_walk function that takes a callback instead of duplicating. The difference from the CPU path: instead of writing to BTreeMap<SiteKey, SiteCounts>, emit Observation values. The max_depth cap during scanning is NOT applied here — depth capping happens during count materialization in aggregate.rs after GPU readback, since the GPU counts are additive. Frontier is computed using TargetFrontierIndex::frontier_for_record. Progress events use try_send to avoid blocking the scanner on a slow aggregator.
close_reason: Added feature-gated gpu/scan.rs with parallel BAM scan worker spawning, bounded scan events, best-effort progress, and observation emission from CIGAR/base walking. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Implement gpu/aggregate.rs — chunk plan, GPU execution, and count materialization
description:
Create src/call_targets/gpu/aggregate.rs to own the chunking strategy and the per-chunk GPU execution + CPU result extraction.

## ChunkPlan struct
```rust
pub(crate) struct ChunkPlan {
    pub(crate) max_sites_per_chunk: usize,
    pub(crate) total_chunks: usize,
    pub(crate) per_site_bytes: usize,  // sample_count * 4 * 4
}
```

## build_chunk_plan(site_count, sample_count, matrix_budget_bytes) -> Result<ChunkPlan>
```
per_site_bytes = sample_count * 4 * size_of::<u32>() = sample_count * 16
max_sites_per_chunk = matrix_budget_bytes / per_site_bytes  (minimum 1)
total_chunks = site_count.div_ceil(max_sites_per_chunk)
```
Bail if per_site_bytes == 0 (zero samples). Log a warning if total_chunks > 1 (chunked mode).

## chunk_for_site(site_idx, max_sites_per_chunk) -> usize
site_idx / max_sites_per_chunk — maps each observation to its chunk during scan

## chunk_site_range(chunk_idx, max_sites_per_chunk, site_count) -> (usize, usize)
Start = chunk_idx * max_sites_per_chunk
End = min(start + max_sites_per_chunk, site_count)

## GpuChunkState struct
Per-chunk mutable state during aggregation:
```rust
pub(crate) struct GpuChunkState {
    pub(crate) pending_obs: Vec<Observation>,  // buffered observations awaiting dispatch
    pub(crate) counts_buffer: wgpu::Buffer,    // pre-allocated GPU count matrix (zeroed)
    site_start: u32,
    site_end: u32,
}
```

## flush_chunk(state, kernel, runtime, site_keys, sample_count, max_depth) -> Result<BTreeMap<SiteKey, SiteCounts>>
1. Dispatch kernel for remaining pending_obs in sub-batches
2. Readback counts_buffer:
   a. Create staging buffer (MAP_READ | COPY_DST, same size)
   b. encode copy_buffer_to_buffer(counts_buffer → staging)
   c. Submit and poll(Maintain::Wait)
   d. Map staging buffer (map_async + poll), read u32 slice
3. Materialize: for each site in [site_start, site_end), read sample_count*4 u32s, build SiteCounts only for sites with nonzero counts, apply depth cap via merge_sample_counts_with_cap
4. Return BTreeMap for the chunk's variant sites

## create_chunk_states(chunk_plan, kernel, runtime, sample_count) -> Result<Vec<GpuChunkState>>
Pre-allocate all chunks' counts_buffers upfront. Each is STORAGE | COPY_SRC, size = chunk_site_count * sample_count * 4 * 4 bytes. Zero-initialize with queue.write_buffer of a zeros slice.
notes: The readback staging buffer can be created per flush rather than pre-allocated — it is only used briefly. The counts_buffer must be zeroed before each chunk starts; since each chunk has its own pre-allocated buffer, no zeroing is needed between runs within a single invocation. merge_sample_counts_with_cap is already in pileup.rs as a private function — consider making it pub(crate) so aggregate.rs can reuse it, or duplicate the logic here. The materialization step only emits sites where at least one sample has nonzero counts, keeping the BTreeMap sparse.
close_reason: Added feature-gated gpu/aggregate.rs with chunk planning, count-buffer allocation, GPU flush/readback, sparse materialization, and tests. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Implement gpu/kernel.rs — WGSL aggregate shader and bind group dispatch
notes: The counts_buffer must be created with STORAGE | COPY_SRC usage. A staging buffer (MAP_READ | COPY_DST) is needed to read results back to CPU — create it per-chunk readback rather than persistently. The bind group must be recreated per dispatch since counts_buffer changes per chunk. obs_buffer and params_buffer can be reused across dispatches within a chunk. Use queue.write_buffer for writes (avoids staging buffer for inputs). device.poll(Maintain::Wait) is a blocking synchronization point — it waits for all submitted GPU work to complete before returning.
close_reason: Added feature-gated gpu/kernel.rs with WGSL aggregate shader, persistent upload buffers, dispatch wrapper, count matrix sizing, and feature tests.

title: Implement gpu/runtime.rs — wgpu adapter init and GPU tier classification
description:
Create src/call_targets/gpu/runtime.rs (gated behind #[cfg(feature = 'wgpu')]) to handle wgpu device initialization and auto-tune parameters based on GPU capability.

## GpuRuntime struct
```rust
pub(crate) struct GpuRuntime {
    pub(crate) device: wgpu::Device,
    pub(crate) queue: wgpu::Queue,
    pub(crate) adapter_info: wgpu::AdapterInfo,
    pub(crate) limits: wgpu::Limits,
}
```

## try_initialize_gpu(backend_mask: wgpu::Backends, verbose: u8) -> Result<Option<GpuRuntime>>
1. Create wgpu::Instance with given backends
2. Request high-performance adapter (compatible_surface: None)
3. Request device with default limits — no extra features needed
4. Return None (not Err) if no compatible adapter found; Err only on device creation failure

## GpuTier enum
```rust
pub(crate) enum GpuTier {
    Datacenter,        // H100, A100, L40
    HighEndDiscrete,   // RTX 4090, RTX 3090, A6000
    Discrete,          // other dGPUs
    IntegratedOrLaptop,
}
```

## classify_adapter(info: &wgpu::AdapterInfo) -> GpuTier
Match adapter name (case-insensitive) against known high-end GPU names. Default to Discrete for unknown discrete GPUs, IntegratedOrLaptop for integrated/software.

## GpuAutoTuning struct — default parameters by tier
```rust
pub(crate) struct GpuAutoTuning {
    pub(crate) stream_matrix_budget_bytes: usize,  // how much GPU storage for count matrix
    pub(crate) max_obs_upload: usize,              // max observations per GPU dispatch
    pub(crate) ready_batch_obs_limit: usize,       // batch size before triggering dispatch
}
```

Defaults by tier:
| Tier               | matrix_budget | max_obs_upload | ready_limit |
|--------------------|---------------|----------------|-------------|
| Datacenter         | 1 GiB         | 64M            | 750k        |
| HighEndDiscrete    | 512 MiB       | 32M            | 350k        |
| Discrete           | 256 MiB       | 24M            | 220k        |
| IntegratedOrLaptop | 128 MiB       | 16M            | 120k        |

## effective_matrix_budget(limits, requested_budget) -> usize
Cap requested budget to min(max_storage_buffer_binding_size, max_buffer_size, requested_budget). Both limits must be queried from device.limits() after device creation.
notes: Use wgpu::util::initialize_adapter_from_env_or_default or the manual request_adapter path. Prefer manual to control power preference. The adapter_info.device_type field (DiscreteGpu, IntegratedGpu, VirtualGpu, Cpu) supplements name-matching for tier classification. Do NOT use async/await — use pollster::block_on or futures::executor::block_on to drive the async wgpu calls synchronously (add pollster as a dev-dep or use the futures crate already in the tree).
close_reason: Added feature-gated gpu/runtime.rs with wgpu adapter initialization, GPU tier classification, auto-tuning defaults, budget capping, and feature tests.

title: Implement observation.rs — packed observation format and target site map
description:
Create src/call_targets/observation.rs with the core data structures shared between CPU scan workers and GPU aggregation.

## Observation struct
```rust
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Observation {
    pub(crate) site_idx: u32,      // index into sorted target site array
    pub(crate) sample_base: u32,   // (sample_idx << 2) | base_idx (A=0,C=1,G=2,T=3)
}
```

## TargetSiteMap
Pre-built O(1) lookup structure from target intervals:
```rust
pub(crate) struct TargetSiteMap {
    lookup: HashMap<u64, u32>,   // packed (ref_id << 32 | pos1) → site_idx
    pub(crate) site_keys: Vec<SiteKey>,  // sorted by (ref_id, position)
    target_refs: HashSet<usize>,         // which ref IDs have any target
}
```

## build_target_site_map(targets: &TargetIndex) -> Result<TargetSiteMap>
Expand every position within every target interval into an individual site. Iterate refs in sorted order, then positions in order, assigning a monotonically increasing site_idx. Store packed key = (ref_id as u64) << 32 | position (1-based) in the hashmap.

Validate site count fits in u32 (bail if > u32::MAX >> 2 to leave headroom for sample packing).

## site_index(map, ref_id, pos1) -> Option<u32>
Pack the key and do a hashmap lookup. Returns None for off-target positions.

## TargetFrontierIndex
Used by scan workers to report their progress through sorted sites:
```rust
pub(crate) struct TargetFrontierIndex {
    ref_ranges: HashMap<usize, (usize, usize)>,  // ref_id → (start_idx, end_idx) in site_keys
}
```
build_target_frontier_index(site_keys, ref_count) builds the ref_ranges.
frontier_for_record(index, ref_id, pos1) returns the site_idx of the first site >= pos1 on that ref (binary search within ref_ranges). This is the scan frontier: all sites below this index are guaranteed to have been passed by the scanner.
notes: This module does NOT depend on wgpu and should compile without the wgpu feature. It is used by both the GPU scan workers and potentially by a future streaming CPU path. The packed key (ref_id << 32 | pos1) uses 1-based positions consistent with SAM/VCF convention. Keep build_target_site_map close to load_targets in its API shape — it takes a TargetIndex, not raw BED paths.
close_reason: Added observation.rs with packed observations, target site map/frontier index, and focused tests migrated from the genemancer GPU design.

title: Add wgpu feature flag to Cargo.toml
description:
Gate the GPU calling path behind a Cargo feature flag so the binary compiles without any GPU dependencies by default.

Add to Cargo.toml:
  [features]
  default = []
  wgpu = ['dep:wgpu']

  [dependencies]
  wgpu = { version = '24', optional = true }

The version should match or exceed what genemancer uses (28 as of reference). Pick the latest stable that compiles cleanly. All GPU modules must be wrapped in #[cfg(feature = 'wgpu')] and the call-targets-gpu subcommand must be conditionally compiled.

Cargo.lock should be updated accordingly.
notes: Check current wgpu version at crates.io before pinning. The wgpu crate pulls in a large dependency tree (naga, ash, metal, dx12 platform crates) so expect longer compile times with the feature enabled. Document the feature in CLAUDE.md build commands section.
close_reason: Added default-off wgpu feature, optional wgpu 28 dependency, Cargo.lock entries, and documented feature build command. Verified cargo test and cargo check --features wgpu.

title: GPU-accelerated variant calling via wgpu
description:
Add a GPU-accelerated call-targets-gpu subcommand that uses wgpu (Vulkan/Metal/DX12/GL) to aggregate base observations across all BAMs simultaneously, dramatically reducing runtime on large target sets or high-depth samples.

The CPU path aggregates into a BTreeMap<SiteKey, SiteCounts> sequentially, which is memory-bounded and single-threaded per BAM. The GPU path:
1. Pre-indexes all target sites into a flat array (TargetSiteMap) for O(1) site_idx lookup
2. Scans all BAMs in parallel (one thread per BAM), emitting packed 8-byte observations
3. Routes observations to GPU memory chunks based on site_idx / max_sites_per_chunk
4. Dispatches a WGSL atomicAdd kernel to count base observations per (site, sample, base)
5. Reads back the count matrix, materializes variant sites, and streams chunks to a separate writer thread

Falls back to the CPU streaming path if no GPU adapter is available (unless --require-gpu is set). CUDA is out of scope for the initial implementation; wgpu provides cross-platform GPU support (Vulkan, Metal, DX12, OpenGL).
design:
Module layout:
  src/call_targets/observation.rs    — Observation struct, TargetSiteMap, packed key
  src/call_targets/gpu/mod.rs        — run_gpu() orchestration
  src/call_targets/gpu/runtime.rs    — wgpu adapter/device init, GpuRuntime, tier classification
  src/call_targets/gpu/kernel.rs     — WGSL shader, bind group layout, kernel dispatch
  src/call_targets/gpu/aggregate.rs  — ChunkPlan, CPU count extraction, per-chunk GPU execution
  src/call_targets/gpu/scan.rs       — parallel scan workers, ScanEvent channel
  src/call_targets/gpu/progress.rs   — ProgressCounters, reporter thread

main.rs: CallTargetsGpuArgs (extends CallTargetsArgs with GPU flags), Command::CallTargetsGpu

Compile-time: wgpu is gated behind a 'wgpu' feature flag in Cargo.toml.
close_reason: Wired feature-gated call-targets-gpu command with backend selection, GPU initialization/fallback, target site expansion, parallel scan observation routing, GPU chunk aggregation, and existing VCF output. Verified cargo test, cargo test --features wgpu, and call-targets-gpu --help.

title: Add GPU paired calling output parity
description: Ensure call-targets-gpu uses the same paired classification/output behavior as CPU call-targets.
design: Reuse the shared output writer/classifier from CPU so GPU aggregated SiteCounts follow identical paired thresholds and INFO output. Add feature-gated tests around writer/classifier where possible rather than GPU hardware tests.
acceptance_criteria: call-targets-gpu paired mode has the same CLI and output semantics as CPU paired mode; cargo test --features wgpu passes.
close_reason: Added explicit GPU paired output parity coverage through the shared writer used by call-targets-gpu. The feature-gated test writes a paired GPU-labeled VCF, verifies paired INFO headers/record annotations and CSI index creation, and README now documents paired CPU/GPU examples and INFO fields. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Add expression-based VCF filtering
description: Extend varlock filter beyond shortcut flags with an expression language over INFO fields and eventually FORMAT/sample fields.
design: Define a small predicate AST for comparisons, boolean operators, missing values, and numeric/string literals. Start with INFO-only expressions such as 'gnomAD_AF < 0.01 && DP >= 20', then reuse the same evaluator for FORMAT/sample predicates later.
acceptance_criteria: filter supports --expr for INFO predicates; tests cover numeric/string/missing comparisons and boolean operators; shortcut flags remain supported.
close_reason: Added INFO expression filtering with --expr. Expressions support INFO field presence, numeric and quoted string literals, ==/!=/</<=/>/>=, &&, ||, !, parentheses, and missing(FIELD); repeated --expr flags combine with AND alongside existing shortcut filters. Added unit and VCF streaming tests plus CLI help and README examples. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Add sample-aware VCF filtering
description: Extend varlock filter to inspect FORMAT fields and sample groups for genotype/depth/allele-state predicates.
design: Add --sample-group NAME=a,b and FORMAT predicate helpers such as sample has alt, min sample DP, affected.any(), unaffected.all(), and genotype-state checks. Preserve selected samples in output initially; projection can be a later option.
acceptance_criteria: filter can evaluate basic FORMAT predicates for named samples/groups; tests cover GT and DP predicates across multi-sample VCF records.
close_reason: Added sample-aware VCF filtering. filter now supports --sample-group, per-sample GT/DP predicates, sample alternate-allele checks, and group any/all predicates over FORMAT/GT and FORMAT/DP while preserving all samples in output. Header validation reports missing samples or groups early. Added unit and VCF streaming tests plus CLI help and README examples. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Clean up Cargo include list
description: Format and commit the Cargo.toml package include list now that tests/ exists.
acceptance_criteria: Cargo.toml include list is idiomatically formatted; cargo check passes; change is committed.
close_reason: Formatted and committed the Cargo.toml package include list now that tests/ exists. Verified cargo check.

title: Add simple integration tests
description: Add a small tests/ integration test suite for basic CLI behavior and annotate smoke coverage.
acceptance_criteria: tests/ contains simple integration tests; cargo test passes.
close_reason: Added tests/cli_smoke.rs with simple binary-level integration coverage for top-level help, annotate help, and an annotate smoke test that writes a bgzipped VCF plus default CSI index from tiny VCF fixtures. Verified cargo test and cargo test --test cli_smoke.

title: Add reference-normalized annotation matching
description: Extend varlock annotate with optional reference-aware normalization so equivalent VCF allele representations can match annotation database records.
design: Add --reference to annotate for left-normalization. Normalize CHROM/POS/REF/ALT keys for input and database records before exact matching. Preserve original output records. Handle indels carefully and keep symbolic alleles unsupported or explicitly skipped until defined.
acceptance_criteria: annotate can match normalized equivalent records when --reference is supplied; behavior without --reference remains exact-key; tests cover simple indel left-normalization and unsupported symbolic alleles.
close_reason: Added optional reference-normalized annotation matching. varlock annotate now accepts --reference, normalizes database and input keys when a reference is supplied, preserves original output records, left-shifts simple indels in repeated sequence, and leaves symbolic/special alleles unchanged. Normalized mode loads databases into memory so all database keys can be normalized before matching. Added tests for left-shifted indel matching and symbolic allele handling, and updated README/help smoke coverage. Verified cargo test, cargo test --features wgpu, and annotate --help.

title: Add CSI database lookup for annotate
description: Extend varlock annotate database lookup to use adjacent .csi indexes in addition to .tbi tabix indexes.
design: Use noodles_csi indexed reader against VCF-compatible CSI headers. Detect DB .csi when no .tbi is present, query by CHROM:POS-POS, and preserve the current exact CHROM/POS/REF/ALT filtering after region lookup. Add tests with a CSI-indexed annotation database.
acceptance_criteria: annotate uses .csi database indexes when available; .tbi remains supported; unindexed database fallback remains unchanged; tests cover CSI lookup.
close_reason: Added CSI annotation database lookup. annotate now detects adjacent .csi indexes when .tbi is absent, opens them with noodles_csi, queries by CHROM:POS-POS, and applies the same exact CHROM/POS/REF/ALT filtering as the TBI path. Added a regression test for CSI-indexed database lookup and updated README. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Add indexed annotation output and lookup
description: Extend varlock annotate beyond the initial in-memory exact-key implementation by writing an output CSI/TBI index and using indexed database lookups instead of loading whole VCF databases into memory.
design: Reuse output indexing patterns from call_targets/output.rs for annotated VCF output. For databases, prefer bgzipped/indexed VCF querying by region when a database index is available, with an explicit fallback or error for unindexed databases. Preserve exact key matching initially. Add --index-type csi|tbi for annotate output.
acceptance_criteria: annotate writes a VCF.gz plus requested index; indexed database lookup is available for bgzipped/indexed VCF databases; tests cover indexed output and at least one indexed lookup path.
close_reason: Implemented annotate output indexing and tabix-indexed database lookup. varlock annotate now accepts --index-type csi|tbi, writes the requested output index, uses adjacent .tbi indexes for database region lookup when present, and falls back to in-memory database loading otherwise. Added tests for CSI output, TBI output, and tabix database lookup. CSI database lookup is tracked separately in varlock-h6p.

title: Add annotation normalization and multi-ALT support
description: Extend varlock annotate to support normalized variant keys and multi-ALT records in input and annotation databases.
design: Add optional --reference for left-normalization and exact allele normalization. Split multi-ALT records for matching while preserving record output. Handle INFO fields with Number=A carefully when mapping database annotations. Decide behavior for symbolic and non-SNV alleles.
acceptance_criteria: annotate can match normalized equivalent records when requested; multi-ALT input/database behavior is defined and tested; Number=A INFO mapping is correct for selected alleles.
close_reason: Implemented the multi-ALT portion of annotation support. Database records now split by ALT, comma-valued mapped fields with one value per ALT are selected by ALT index, input multi-ALT records are preserved, and output annotations are emitted as Number=A comma-aligned INFO values with . for missing ALT annotations. Added tests for multi-ALT database parsing, full multi-ALT annotation, and partial multi-ALT misses. Reference-normalized matching was split into varlock-vtx for a focused reference-aware implementation. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Plan paired sample calling mode
description: Plan a paired calling mode for tumor/normal or case/control style BAM inputs where variants are evaluated using two related samples rather than only pooled global evidence.
design: Proposed mode: extend call-targets and call-targets-gpu with explicit sample roles such as --pair tumor=Tumor,normal=Normal or --tumor-sample/--normal-sample. Paired calling should evaluate alternate evidence in the case/tumor sample while using the matched control/normal to classify or filter events. Start with SNV logic matching current A/C/G/T caller: tumor alt count/fraction thresholds, normal max alt count/fraction thresholds, optional minimum normal depth, and output INFO/FORMAT fields describing paired classification. Later extend to multiple pairs or case/control groups.
acceptance_criteria: Issue design covers CLI shape, sample-role resolution, thresholds, output fields, behavior with multi-sample BAM/VCF output, CPU/GPU implications, examples, and implementation phases.
notes: Examples: varlock call-targets --input paired.bam --reference hg38.fa --targets panel.bed --pair tumor=Tumor,normal=Normal --tumor-min-alt-count 3 --tumor-min-alt-fraction 0.05 --normal-max-alt-count 0 --normal-max-alt-fraction 0.01. For separate BAMs: use --rg-map or existing SM tags to assign Tumor/Normal roles. Output should keep both samples and add INFO fields such as PAIR=Tumor/Normal, SOMATIC=1, TUMOR_AF, NORMAL_AF, TUMOR_ALT_COUNT, NORMAL_ALT_COUNT. Phases: sample role validation; paired filter/classifier over existing SiteCounts; CPU output fields; GPU path parity; multiple-pair manifest support.
close_reason: Planned paired sample calling mode and split it into implementation beads. Initial scope is one tumor/normal pair via --pair tumor=SAMPLE,normal=SAMPLE, with tumor min alt count/fraction, normal max alt count/fraction, optional min normal depth, CPU classification/output INFO fields, then GPU parity through the shared output path. Implementation beads: varlock-ejs for CLI and role validation, varlock-4h4 for CPU classification/output, varlock-pvh for GPU parity.

title: Plan post-annotation VCF filtering
description: Plan a future filtering layer that runs after variant annotation and filters one or more-sample VCFs using annotation-derived fields, allele evidence, sample/genotype state, and database frequency thresholds.
design: Proposed command: varlock filter --input annotated.vcf.gz --output filtered.vcf.gz with expression-based filtering over INFO, FORMAT, genotype state, sample groups, and annotation namespaces. It should work as a standalone VCF filter and as a natural follow-up to varlock annotate. Support simple threshold flags for common use cases, plus a more expressive predicate syntax for complex filters. Filtering must preserve and update VCF headers and output a bgzipped VCF with CSI/TBI index.
acceptance_criteria: Issue design covers CLI shape, expression language or predicate model, annotation namespace access, sample/group-aware filtering, common frequency filters, output/header behavior, examples, and implementation phases.
notes: Examples: varlock filter --input annotated.vcf.gz --expr 'gnomad_AF < 0.01 && DP >= 20' --output rare.vcf.gz; varlock filter --input annotated.vcf.gz --sample-group affected=a,b --sample-group unaffected=c,d --expr 'affected.any(GT != "0/0") && unaffected.all(GT == "0/0") && db.common_AF < 0.001'. Common shortcut flags could include --max-frequency namespace:field=value, --require-info FIELD, --drop-info FIELD, --sample-has-alt SAMPLE, and --min-sample-dp SAMPLE:DP. Phases: define predicate AST; implement INFO-only filters; add FORMAT/sample predicates; add annotation namespace helpers; add index-preserving streaming output; add docs/tests.
close_reason: Implemented the first post-annotation filtering slice. Added varlock filter with INFO-only predicates: --require-info, --exclude-info, and repeatable --max-info FIELD=VALUE. Filter streams plain or gzipped VCF text, preserves headers, writes bgzipped VCF output plus CSI/TBI index, and treats comma-valued numeric INFO fields as pass only when all non-missing values are <= threshold. Added unit tests and CLI smoke coverage, and updated README. Expression filtering and sample-aware FORMAT filtering were split into follow-up beads. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Plan VCF variant intersection and difference
description: Plan a future subcommand for variant set operations across two single-sample VCFs, multi-sample VCFs, and multiple multi-sample files. The feature must support intersection and difference with explicit sample/file selection semantics.
design: Proposed command: varlock intersect with subcommands or modes for intersection and difference. Use explicit operands rather than implicit sample names. Variant identity should be normalized as (CHROM, POS, REF, ALT) after optional left-normalization against a reference; default matching should be site+allele, with optional --site-only and --genotype-aware modes. For two single-sample files: varlock intersect --left tumor.vcf.gz --right normal.vcf.gz --mode shared|left-only|right-only. For one multi-sample file with samples a b c d: allow --left-samples a,b --right-samples c,d and compute shared or difference across sample groups. For multiple multi-sample files: allow repeated --set NAME=vcf.gz:sample1,sample2 or a manifest file; expression support can come later, starting with --mode all-shared, any-shared, left-only, and set-diff A-B. Output should be VCF preserving selected samples plus INFO fields describing membership/support. Implementation phases: VCF parser/index model; variant key normalization; two-file single-sample set ops; sample group ops within one VCF; multi-file manifest support; streaming/indexed performance.
acceptance_criteria: Issue design describes CLI shape, data model, matching semantics, examples for two single-sample files, one multi-sample file with samples a b c d, and multiple multi-sample files, plus implementation phases.
notes: Need decisions: exact VCF crate, normalization behavior for indels, whether missing genotypes count as absence, and whether output is a projected VCF or tabular summary by default.

title: Plan VCF variant annotation databases
description: Plan a future annotation subcommand that adds database annotations to one or more-sample VCFs using one or more variant/frequency databases.
design: Proposed command: varlock annotate --input calls.vcf.gz --database db.vcf.gz --database gnomad.vcf.gz --output annotated.vcf.gz. Databases may initially be bgzipped/indexed VCF-like resources with INFO frequency fields; later support BED/TSV interval or variant-key databases through typed adapters. Matching should default to exact normalized allele key (CHROM, POS, REF, ALT), with optional --site-only for site annotations. Allow field mapping such as --annotation gnomad:AF=gnomAD_AF,AC=gnomAD_AC and automatic header insertion. Multiple databases should be namespaced and deterministic; conflicts are resolved by namespace, not overwrite. Output remains streaming VCF.gz with CSI/TBI index and provenance header lines for each database. Implementation phases: annotation database abstraction; indexed VCF database lookup; INFO/header writer; multi-database namespacing; frequency-specific shortcuts; tests with one-sample and multi-sample VCFs.
acceptance_criteria: Issue design describes CLI shape, supported input database classes, annotation field configuration, multi-database behavior, output/header semantics, examples, and implementation phases.
notes: Implementation started with a dependency-light first slice: exact allele-key annotation over VCF-like text. Scope for this slice: varlock annotate --input calls.vcf.gz --database name=path.vcf.gz --annotation name:SRC=DST --output calls.annotated.vcf.gz. Load database records into maps keyed by CHROM,POS,REF,ALT; copy input records while appending INFO annotations; preserve headers and add INFO/provenance lines. Full indexed lookup, normalization, and TSV/BED adapters remain later phases.
close_reason: Annotation roadmap accepted and split into implementation work. Initial exact-key VCF annotation is tracked in varlock-27s; indexed lookup, normalization, and non-VCF database adapters should be filed as follow-up implementation beads as needed.

title: Shard static-target GPU chunks across adapters
description: Use multiple selected GPU adapters for call-targets-gpu when a target BED is provided by distributing independent target chunks across runtime kernels.
design: After scan assigns observations to target chunks, distribute chunk indices across GPU runtimes, preferably round-robin or by pending observation count. Each runtime flushes its assigned chunks and returns sparse counts. Static target chunks are disjoint by site range, so merging is an ordered extend with no site overlap. Preserve deterministic output order through BTreeMap materialization.
acceptance_criteria: Static target mode can use multiple selected adapters; output matches single-adapter execution on tests; logs show per-adapter chunk/observation counts; tests pass.
close_reason: Static target chunks now allocate buffers on assigned GPU workers and flush through each worker's runtime/kernel. Chunk assignment is round-robin across selected adapters, with chunk planning constrained by the smallest worker matrix budget and verbose per-worker chunk/observation metrics. Verified cargo test and cargo test --features wgpu.

title: Plan multi-GPU aggregation sharding
description: Design how call-targets-gpu should use multiple GPUs concurrently after explicit adapter selection exists. The current implementation uses one wgpu Device/Queue. Multi-GPU support should shard independent target chunks or no-target windows across selected adapters without changing output semantics.
design: After adapter selection lands, introduce a runtime set with one kernel per selected adapter. Static target mode can shard target chunks by chunk index. No-target mode should shard flushed covered batches/windows. Each shard materializes sparse counts and merges through the existing count merger. Guard max-depth semantics by ensuring all observations for a site are assigned deterministically or by merging raw counts before capping. Start with design doc/bead notes before implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Document recommended sharding boundary, merge semantics, CLI shape, and correctness risks; create implementation beads if the design is accepted.
notes: Adapter selection is now the foundation. Recommended next implementation steps: (1) allow selecting more than one adapter with repeated --gpu-index or comma-separated --gpu-indices; (2) represent runtimes as Vec<GpuRuntime>, one kernel per runtime; (3) static target mode can shard independent chunk indices across runtimes; (4) no-target mode should shard coordinate/window flushes, not arbitrary observation batches, to avoid max-depth order effects; (5) merge raw or uncapped counts before applying max-depth if a site can cross shard boundaries; (6) add deterministic tests comparing single-GPU and sharded outputs on synthetic counts before enabling multi-GPU execution by default.
close_reason: Recorded multi-GPU sharding design and split implementation into beads: multi-adapter selection, runtime set, static-target chunk sharding, and no-target coordinate-window correctness. Added dependencies so runtime set waits on selection and static sharding waits on runtime set.

title: Extract call_targets/output.rs — BGZF VCF writing and indexing
description: Move CallTargetsOutputState, WriteMetrics, begin_call_targets_output, write_call_targets_output_chunk, finish_call_targets_output, write_vcf_header, write_vcf_record, choose_alt, and base_index into src/call_targets/output.rs. This module owns the stateful VCF writer: it opens the BGZF file, writes the VCF header, iterates site counts to filter and emit records, and finalises the CSI or TBI index.
notes: choose_alt picks the highest-count non-ref allele across all samples. base_index maps A/C/G/T to 0-3. VCF records must be emitted in BTreeMap iteration order (sorted by SiteKey) — the CSI/TBI indexers require monotonically increasing coordinates. CSI and TBI indexers are mutually exclusive (only one is Some based on IndexType). WriteMetrics tracks ns-resolution timing for fasta_lookup, filter_eval, vcf_write, and index_update stages.
close_reason: Closed

title: Extract call_targets/reference.rs — indexed FASTA random access
description: Move FaiRecord, FastaIndex, FastaReader, FastaLineCache, open_fai, open_fasta_index, and is_bgzf_reference into src/call_targets/reference.rs. FastaIndex provides line-cached random base lookup (fetch_base) into either a plain or BGZF-indexed FASTA. It is used exclusively by CallTargetsOutputState in output.rs to look up reference bases when writing VCF records.
notes: FastaIndex.line_cache stores the last-fetched FASTA line (ref_name + line_index + bases Vec). The cache hit path avoids a seek entirely. FastaIndex is only used in output.rs — make it pub(super) and import it from there.
close_reason: Closed

title: Extract call_targets/pileup.rs — BAM scanning and count aggregation
description: Move ScanParams, PileupSettings, InputResult, process_input_bam, pileup_record, should_skip_record, record_sample, merge_counts, and merge_sample_counts_with_cap into src/call_targets/pileup.rs. This is the largest and most logic-dense grouping — it owns all BAM read iteration, CIGAR walking, base quality filtering, depth capping, and multi-BAM count merging.
notes: merge_sample_counts_with_cap uses proportional truncation with largest-remainder rounding — no behaviour changes allowed. ScanParams and PileupSettings hold references so they have lifetime parameters; keep them in this file. InputResult.skipped_rg and .skipped_flags are only used for verbose logging in run() — they must remain on the struct.
close_reason: Closed

title: Extract call_targets/targets.rs — BED interval loading
description: Move load_targets and in_targets into src/call_targets/targets.rs. load_targets parses a BED file into a TargetIndex (HashMap<ref_id, Vec<Interval>> with merged intervals). in_targets binary-searches a sorted Vec<Interval> for a 0-based position.
notes: in_targets is called from pileup_record in pileup.rs — it will need to be pub(crate) or pub(super) depending on module visibility chosen.
close_reason: Closed

title: Extract call_targets/types.rs — shared data model
description: Move SiteKey, SiteCounts, Interval, TargetIndex, and PreparedCallTargets out of call_targets.rs into src/call_targets/types.rs. These structs have no logic — they are pure data and are referenced across all other sub-modules, so they must be extracted first to avoid circular dependencies.
notes: All five types are currently pub(crate). Mark them pub(crate) in types.rs and re-export via mod.rs if needed. SiteKey derives Ord/Hash so BTreeMap and HashMap keying works — preserve all derives.
close_reason: Closed

title: Extract call_targets/samples.rs — RG/SM resolution
description: Move collect_samples, build_rg_to_sm_from_map, rg_to_sm_from_header, read_rg_map, and insert_rg_sample into src/call_targets/samples.rs. These functions form a cohesive unit: given BAM paths and an optional rg-map file, they produce a (Vec<String>, HashMap<String,String>) of (sample_names, rg_to_sm).
notes: insert_rg_sample is called by both collect_samples (header path) and build_rg_to_sm_from_map (file path). Keep it in this module as pub(super).
close_reason: Closed

title: Refactor call_targets.rs into focused sub-modules
description:
call_targets.rs is ~1450 lines and mixes eight distinct concerns in a single file. Split it into a call_targets/ directory module so each concern lives in its own file. The orchestration (run, prepare_call_targets) stays in mod.rs; everything else moves to purpose-named sub-modules.

Target structure:
  src/call_targets/
    mod.rs        — run(), prepare_call_targets(), write_call_targets_output()
    types.rs      — SiteKey, SiteCounts, Interval, TargetIndex, PreparedCallTargets
    samples.rs    — collect_samples, rg_to_sm_from_header, read_rg_map, insert_rg_sample, build_rg_to_sm_from_map
    targets.rs    — load_targets, in_targets
    pileup.rs     — ScanParams, PileupSettings, InputResult, process_input_bam, pileup_record, should_skip_record, record_sample, merge_counts, merge_sample_counts_with_cap
    reference.rs  — FaiRecord, FastaIndex, FastaReader, FastaLineCache, open_fai, open_fasta_index, is_bgzf_reference
    output.rs     — CallTargetsOutputState, WriteMetrics, begin_call_targets_output, write_call_targets_output_chunk, finish_call_targets_output, write_vcf_header, write_vcf_record, choose_alt, base_index

No behaviour changes — only file organisation.
design: Convert src/call_targets.rs to src/call_targets/mod.rs and extract each concern into a sibling file. Use pub(super) for items only needed within the call_targets module tree, pub(crate) for items referenced from outside (currently: run, prepare_call_targets, write_call_targets_output, begin_call_targets_output, write_call_targets_output_chunk, finish_call_targets_output, CallTargetsOutputState, SiteKey, SiteCounts, TargetIndex, PreparedCallTargets). Verify with cargo build and cargo clippy after each file extraction.
close_reason: Closed
